title: The listing record, its publication channels, its price schedule and its pause marker have no legacy Data row, no list value and no owner operation, and the plan carries no requirement id
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E3-029, its Story, Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4, Data, Endpoints, Screen and states and Permission checks tables); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature row FEAT-AST-12 Publish the listing, System, runs unattended, systems HOME.SCB and auction portals, depends on FEAT-AST-11); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-33, R-DIS-67, with R-DIS-32, R-DIS-34, R-DIS-35 and R-DIS-68 as the adjacent rules of the same machine); Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6 (CREATE TABLE listing, asset_sale, with the comment business key; no foreign key); Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008, LOV-SALE-CHANNEL, LOV-LISTING, DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219, DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045, DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018, DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 (REQ-S5-005); _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows of S5: two tables, six REST operations, one event, one job, one workflow); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (both slices of RWB-E3-029, the C list empty and reqs empty)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 1, 3, 4, 8, 9, 11; s7 Acceptance criteria note; s8 BR1, BR3, BR4, BR5, BR6; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.2; s12.8; s13 Solution plan; s18 Traceability; s19 Out of scope; CON s2, s3, s7 AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, s11 Data, s12.2, s12.8, s13, s18, s19
description: The feature writes a listing and the legacy story records five data rows, none of which is the listing: recovery_case, deviation, v_ace_npa_asset, decision_log_entry and rule_row. The listing record therefore has to be read from the physical schema and the data model, where it exists as listing with DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008 (id, asset_key, sale_channel, start_price, floor_price, round_no, listed_at, status) and is owned by S5 in rwb_asset. Three facts the criteria use have no place in that record. First, AC2 publishes to three channels (HOME.SCB, the EASY app and the auction portal) while sale_channel holds one value per row and LOV-SALE-CHANNEL holds only DUTCH_AUCTION, BROKER, DIRECT, LED_AUCTION and RAMC, so neither HOME.SCB nor the EASY app has a list value and the mapping of a channel to a value is a parameter of the publication, not a decision of the build. Second, the price schedule of AC1 and AC3 is a payload of the publication and has no column and no schedule table, its steps being R-DIS-36 and R-DIS-38's. Third, the pause of R-DIS-67 has no state: LOV-LISTING gives DRAFT, LIVE, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD and WITHDRAWN and no paused value, so the pause marker is held in the free-text state column of listing and its value is not specified. The evidence facts of R-DIS-33 (photographs_count, inspection_report, title_status) and the deviation codes of R-DIS-67 are the facts of rwb-document, rwb-source-data and rwb-deviation and no source names the operation that answers them. The legacy key also carries no requirement id and the plan's reqs list for both slices is empty, while REQ-S5-005 (Listings are published to the bank's channel and the auction portal from one action) names exactly the outcome of AC2. No business value is invented: the channel mapping, the pause marker value and the three consumed operation names carry the placeholder and are settled at the baseline review.
evidence: The Data table of RWB-E3-029 lists recovery_case, deviation, v_ace_npa_asset, decision_log_entry and rule_row only; the physical schema defines listing with eight business columns and no channel, schedule or pause column; the LOV rows give LOV-SALE-CHANNEL five values and LOV-LISTING five values, neither of which covers HOME.SCB, the EASY app or a paused listing; the rule rows R-DIS-33 and R-DIS-67 name photographs_count, inspection_report, title_status and deviation_open, which no table of rwb_asset holds; the split plan gives reqs as an empty list for RWB-S5-E3029-APP and -CON; Business Requirements Program v4 gives REQ-S5-005 for the publication.
area: Data model, channels and traceability, S5 rwb-asset
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the data steward and the business analyst
proposed: Keep listing and DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008 as the record, declare the channel mapping and the pause marker as reference data at their version, read the evidence and the deviation on their owners' contracts, and let step D1 add REQ-S5-005 to the reqs list of both slices.

title: The publication to HOME.SCB, the EASY app and the auction portal has no owner contract in the plan, DP-16 is not in the pattern set, and the publish request and answer have no published shape
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 (slide 19 rwb-asset IN and OUT: REST GET/POST /assets, /listings; EVT JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult, ProceedsMatched; TMP AssetDisposalWorkflow; topic rwb.asset.events.v1 with AssetTakenOn and AssetSold; TMP Partner: issueInstruction (auction vendor); slide 13 connection matrix, row S5 Asset; the appendix service row S5); _work/msr/context/S5.md (six REST operations provided, one event, ownership rows of S5); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (patterns DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19 and the C list empty for both slices); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (FEAT-AST-12 systems HOME.SCB and auction portals); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-33 systems HOME.SCB and auction portal)
section: CON s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 1, 3; s7 AC1, AC3, AC4; s8 BR5, BR6, BR9; s11 Data; s12.1; s12.2; s12.8; s13 Solution plan; s19 Out of scope; APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 9; s5 X5; s12.2; s12.8; s13 Solution plan; s19
description: The two criteria of the feature send a listing to three outside channels, and the architecture gives the service neither an adapter nor a contract for them. Architecture v5 slide 19 gives rwb-asset the REST operations GET and POST /assets and /listings, the Temporal calls Partner: issueInstruction (auction vendor), Decision: child: approval and Payment: postProceeds, and no channel publication of any kind; the plan's pattern set for this key carries DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 only, so DP-16 (rwb-integration contract) is absent together with its C row RWB-P2-E1007-CON, and the C list of both slices is empty. HOME.SCB and the EASY app are bank channels that no slide, no ownership row and no feature row assigns to a service. The publish request, its answer, the entry per channel and the pause command therefore have no published shape: they are declared in the baseline with the placeholder, built against a fake on Day 1, and the publication is consumed as the rwb-integration contract rather than built as an adapter of rwb-asset. The case move is likewise answered on the rwb-case contract and not carried by an event, because the topic of the service holds AssetTakenOn and AssetSold only and neither is a listing event.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 19 rwb-asset IN and OUT gives no channel call and names rwb-integration nowhere; the connection matrix row S5 Asset has no cell to P2 and no cell to an outside system; the split plan patterns of RWB-S5-E3029-APP and -CON are DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 with C empty; FEAT-AST-12 gives HOME.SCB and auction portals as systems with no owner; R-DIS-33 gives the same two systems; no published OpenAPI or AsyncAPI of rwb-asset exists in the extract set.
owner_role: Integration architect with the P2 rwb-integration service owner and the S5 rwb-asset service owner
proposed: Declare the publication and the pause as consumed rows of the P2 rwb-integration contract with a placeholder, build against its fake on Day 1, and let step D1 add C RWB-P2-E1007-CON and DP-16 to the pattern set of both slices.

title: The module FSD and TSD extracts named by the work package are absent from the run extract set, so the module section citations of the fill order are not available
source: _work/msr/wp/B2-S5-011.md (Read only: _work/msr/extract/ files of the FSD and TSD folders whose name contains S5, module Asset); _work/msr/extract (the listing of the folder: no file whose name contains S5); Template and Rules v1 R7.3 (fill order for thin stories); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature rows of S5); Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6; _work/msr/context/S5.md
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s8 Business rules; s11 Data; s13 Solution plan; CON s2, s11, s13
description: The work package names the FSD and TSD extracts of module S5 as the second and third source of the fill order, and no file in _work/msr/extract has S5 in its name, so the two module specifications were not available to this work package. The module facts of both stories are therefore taken from the sources that are present: the legacy story, the feature rows of the Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3, the rule rows of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, the field and list rows of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and the table definitions of the Physical Schema v6. No module section number of the FSD S5 or the TSD S5 is cited in either story, so no citation points at a document that was not read, and no business value is invented to fill the gap.
evidence: The extract folder holds the architecture, the rule, the data model, the physical schema, the batch, the event, the decision log and the BRD extracts, and no FSD or TSD extract of any module; the work package lists them under Read only with the filter whose name contains S5; neither story cites a TSD S5 or FSD S5 section.
owner_role: Realignment coordinator with the S5 module business analyst
proposed: Add the FSD S5 and TSD S5 extracts to the run extract set before the verification loop and let it re-check the module section citations of both stories then.
